findings.assertion: INAH historian Gabriela Sánchez Reyes reports a Franciscan lot assigned in the former Mexica sacred precinct on 2 June 1524 and offered for sale by May 1525; this short tenure does not establish a completed substantial monastery.
findings.limitations: Municipal cabildo originals and mapped lot boundaries not examined

findings.assertion: The criminal sentence arising from the 1566 Alonso de Ávila Alvarado affair included demolition of his house and erection of an inscribed stone warning about treason; the later fate of this plot formed part of the colonial urban history near Templo Mayor.
findings.limitations: Primary trial and punishment documents were not independently reviewed; exact geographic reconstruction tentative

findings.assertion: Sánchez Reyes reports a royal grant dated 1 July 1574 for the former Ávila property to support educational construction associated with the Royal University; grant date should not be confused with documented completion of a university building.
findings.source_locator: Sánchez Reyes 2017 printed p. 13, citing AGN Universidad vol. 7 folios 12–13
findings.limitations: AGN original file not accessed and subsequent property occupation not established

findings.assertion: The demolition of overlying colonial houses began around 1913, but Sánchez Reyes cites a report dated 15 April 1914 in which Manuel Gamio announced locating the ancient pyramid. INAH web pages alternately date excavation to around 1913 and discovery to May 1914.
findings.source_locator: Sánchez Reyes 2017 printed pp. 16–17; INAH PAU closing paragraph; INAH Origen y ombligo closing paragraph
findings.limitations: Conflicting institutional datings; original Gamio field report remains unexamined; distinction between demolition, fieldwork and public announcement provisional

findings.assertion: An approximately 1900 brick wastewater collector was driven across Templo Mayor construction phases, causing destruction in a corridor roughly two metres wide; INAH identifies this modern intervention below the visitor walkway.
findings.source_locator: INAH PAU final paragraph and INAH Templo Mayor Etapa IV y V / Colector de agua
findings.limitations: Original city engineering and archaeological section drawings not inspected; visitor sightline unverified

findings.assertion: Electricity workers encountered the Coyolxauhqui monolith on 21 February 1978 and INAH salvage excavations followed before the broader Proyecto Templo Mayor; 1978 cannot be described as the first-ever excavation of the site.
findings.source_locator: INAH Proyecto Templo Mayor opening paragraph; INAH Lugares archaeological history
findings.limitations: Institutional retellings; original rescue field sheets not examined

findings.assertion: The INAH Programa de Arqueología Urbana was established in 1991 to excavate and study the multiple centuries represented in properties around the former Mexica sacred precinct, including colonial and later deposits.
findings.limitations: Institutional program description; individual post-1991 site reports not yet read

scope: Seven staged historical research findings on colonial precinct properties, Porfirian infrastructure, rediscovery dates and ongoing urban archaeology
